General Motors (GM) has revealed a CarPlay compromise on two truck models, appearing to extend a partial reversal of its decision to drop support for the feature.

A new report says the automaker is developing a truck-specific interface that includes CarPlay……

GM first announced back in 2023 that it was dropping CarPlay from all future electric vehicles, and offered a frankly baffling series of explanations and excuses for the decision. Many customers were understandably upset, and a number said they would never buy another GM vehicle as long as the policy was in effect.

We recently saw the company show the first crack in the CarPlay ban in one of its most expensive luxury EVs, but offered no explanation for the exception.

TNW now reports that the company is developing a brand new in-car infotainment interface for its trucks that supports both CarPlay and Android Auto. The compromise is that they don't get to take over the entire screen.

The company also offered no explanation for this obvious exception, simply saying it wanted to avoid requiring customers to do too much.

The report also discusses growing government concern about the practice of relying on touch screens to control important vehicle functions like horns, windshield wipers, and hazard lights. Both the EU and China now require physical buttons for a number of controls, in order to reduce the amount of time drivers take their eyes off the road to look inside the car.
